subject: ventures/commercial-property-cap-rate-calculator
professional: a senior commercial real estate loan underwriter / small-balance CRE broker who prices 5-50 unit multifamily and strip-retail deals; first checks: is NOI built the way an appraiser builds it (vacancy on rent, management on collected income, reserves above the line), is direct capitalization V = NOI / R applied correctly, is the mortgage constant right against a published amortization table, is the loan sized by the lesser of LTV, DSCR and debt yield as a lender sizes it, and does break-even occupancy match the standard (opex + debt service) / potential income test.

evidence.correctness: Independent Python /tmp/claude-0/audit-commercial-property-cap-rate-calculator/indep.py (no subject import; exact fractions for NOI, the textbook annuity formula checked against the published amortization factor $690.91/mo per $100k at 6.75%/25 yr, break-even occupancy found by bisection on cash flow = 0 rather than the closed form) against node probe.mjs importing the shipped calc.mjs. Sample deal: EGI 229,200, management 11,460, opex 83,460, NOI 145,740, value at 7% 2,082,000, expense ratio 36.41%; debt service 116,073.14, DSCR 1.2556, cash flow 29,666.86, cash-on-cash 4.944%, going-in cap 7.287%, max loan at 1.25x 1,406,258.20, break-even occupancy 79.988%; 0.5-point cap sensitivity 138,800. All match to the cent. Fails at the edges: the sensitivity grid rounds cap rates to one decimal (calc.mjs:37,98), so with a 7.25% cap rate (the input steps by 0.05) the grid's centre column is 7.3% and shows $1,996,438 while the headline value is $2,010,207, and the user's own cap rate is not in the grid; a break-even occupancy above 100% is reported as 'needs about 113% occupancy' with no statement that the deal cannot cover debt even fully leased. Core arithmetic right, edges wrong: 3.
evidence.completeness: Claimed outputs (README, header, rules card): NOI, value at cap rate, going-in cap rate, DSCR, cash-on-cash, break-even occupancy, cap-rate x vacancy grid, text summary, print, usage counting, disclaimer. All present and working in calc.mjs and index.html wiring. One claimed output is conditional: 'the loan a 1.25x lender test allows' (README) / 'the loan a lender is likely to give' (index.html:52) is only rendered when DSCR fails (calc.mjs:120); on the shipped example (DSCR 1.26x) no loan size appears anywhere (findings printed by node -e over compute(SAMPLE)). Served copy builds clean. 3.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the subject: 25/25 pass; the README's repo-root command also 25/25. Six seeded mutants with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py, 2 caught: management term removed from break-even occupancy (caught by the round-trip test), other income moved under vacancy (caught). Survived: vacancy flag threshold 5 -> 3, expense-ratio flag 0.3 -> 0.2, max-loan price cap 0.95 -> 0.75, DSCR finding severity comparison flipped. The test named 'flags ... a low DSCR' (calc.test.mjs:69) never asserts anything about DSCR. Formula engine pinned, every finding threshold unpinned: 2.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (149 lines), index.html (171), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs. Pure functions, input rejected with messages rather than clamped, esc() on all rendered text, no network calls (page.test pins it). Defects: r1() one-decimal rounding of grid cap rates (calc.mjs:37) is a silent precision loss; Math.min(f.breakevenOcc, 9.99) (calc.mjs:121) is an unexplained magic cap; page.test.mjs builds an always-empty `rendered` Set (dead code copied from a template); a test name that overstates what it checks. Small and readable otherwise: 3.
evidence.claims: Checked: FAQ worked example '$145,740 of NOI at a 7% cap rate is about $2.08 million' - pass (2,082,000). 'Runs in your browser; nothing is uploaded' - pass (imports only ./calc.mjs, ./usage.mjs; page.test asserts no fetch/XHR/beacon). Disclaimer and not-an-appraisal text - pass (footer, header note). 'Lenders typically underwrite at least 5% vacancy' - consistent with Fannie Mae / Freddie Mac multifamily minimum 5% economic vacancy practice, uncited but true. 'Multi-tenant property usually runs 35-50%' expense ratio - plausible, uncited. Fail: 'the loan a lender is likely to give' (index.html:52) and 'the loan a 1.25x lender test allows' (README) are shown only when the deal fails 1.25x, and the figure is the DSCR test alone (capped at 95% of price), not a lender's lesser-of-LTV/DSCR/debt-yield sizing. Shipped canonical stays relative './index.html' while the sitemap lists the directory URL (served-copy). One headline claim not backed: 2.
evidence.fitness: Job walked: a small-balance investor screening a $2.0M 7.29%-cap building at 70% LTV gets NOI, value, DSCR 1.26x, 4.9% cash-on-cash and 80% break-even in one click, with a printable summary - a usable first screen. A broker or lender hits gaps in the first hour: no debt yield (NOI / loan, the third sizing test on bank and CMBS loans; 10.4% on the sample), no interest-only period, no loan sizing shown when the deal passes, no multi-year proforma or IRR (honestly listed as not modelled), and a grid that drops their quarter-point cap rate. CoStar/Crexi/Omni calculators give the single-year screen too. 2.
evidence.domain: Compared against direct capitalization as taught in The Appraisal of Real Estate (Appraisal Institute): NOI = EGI - opex with vacancy on potential rent, management on collected income, reserves above the line (appraiser convention; some lenders put them below) - matches. Mortgage constant matches published amortization tables. DSCR 1.25x is a common bank minimum and the page says lenders differ. Departures a senior underwriter would flag: loan sizing ignores debt yield and is not presented as the lesser of LTV and DSCR; break-even occupancy above 100% is not called out as a deal that cannot service its debt; grid omits the input cap rate. 2.

checks.what: Sample NOI build-up and value at a 7% cap rate
checks.method: Direct capitalization (The Appraisal of Real Estate, income approach); exact-fraction Python, no subject import
checks.expected: EGI 229,200; opex 83,460; NOI 145,740; value 2,082,000; expense ratio 36.41%

checks.what: Annual debt service and DSCR on $1.4M at 6.75%, 25 yr
checks.method: Published amortization factor: $690.91/mo per $100k at 6.75% over 25 years (standard mortgage table); annuity formula in Python
Bisection on (GPR x occ + other) x (1 - mgmt) - fixed opex - debt service = 0, not the shipped closed form

checks.what: Max loan at 1.25x DSCR, cash-on-cash and going-in cap
checks.method: Present value of an annuity paying NOI/1.25/12 for 300 months at 0.5625%/mo; CoC = (NOI - DS)/equity; cap = NOI/price

checks.what: Sensitivity grid includes the user's cap rate (7.25%)

checks.method: By hand: a break-even above 100% means the building cannot cover debt service even fully leased
checks.expected: a statement that the deal cannot break even at full occupancy
checks.observed: 'The property needs about 113% occupancy to cover its costs and debt.'

checks.what: Loan size at the 1.25x test shown on the example
checks.expected: a line giving the loan the 1.25x test allows
checks.observed: no loan-size line; maxLoan computed but only rendered when DSCR < 1.25

checks.what: FAQ worked example $145,740 NOI at 7% is about $2.08 million

checks.method: page.test.mjs assertions plus reading the module imports
checks.expected: only local imports; no-warranty and not-an-appraisal text

checks.observed: llms.txt and sitemap rewritten to https://marisstella.app/commercial-property-cap-rate-calculator/; canonical left as relative ./index.html

checks.method: Commercial bank / CMBS practice: loan = lesser of LTV, DSCR and debt-yield constraints
checks.expected: lesser-of sizing with debt yield reported
checks.observed: DSCR constraint capped at 95% of price; no debt yield

mutations.change: egi = p.gpr * (1 - vacancy / 100) + p.otherIncome -> (p.gpr + p.otherIncome) * (1 - vacancy / 100)
severity: f.dscr < LENDER_DSCR ? "high" -> severity: f.dscr > LENDER_DSCR ? "high"

defects.what: The page and README promise 'the loan a lender is likely to give' / 'the loan a 1.25x lender test allows', but the loan size is only rendered when DSCR is below 1.25x; on the shipped example (1.26x) no loan size appears.

Sensitivity grid rounds cap rates to one decimal, so a 7.25% input yields columns 6.3..8.3; the centre column (7.3%, $1,996,438) is not the user's cap rate and disagrees with the headline value ($2,010,207).
Break-even occupancy above 100% is reported as 'needs about 113% occupancy' with no statement that the deal cannot cover debt even fully leased.

4 of 6 seeded mutants survive: the vacancy and expense-ratio flag thresholds, the max-loan price cap and the DSCR finding severity are unpinned; the test named 'flags ... a low DSCR' asserts nothing about DSCR.

Lender loan sizing departs from practice: no debt yield (NOI / loan, a standard bank and CMBS sizing test), no interest-only period, and the max loan is the DSCR test alone rather than the lesser of LTV, DSCR and debt yield.
Shipped canonical is the relative './index.html' (the deploy does not rewrite it) while the sitemap lists the directory URL, two URLs for one page.
Dead code and magic numbers: page.test.mjs builds an always-empty `rendered` Set; Math.min(breakevenOcc, 9.99) caps the display at 999% without explanation.

verdict: A small, clean, private single-year income-approach calculator whose core arithmetic is right: an independent exact-fraction Python recomputation (direct capitalization, the 6.75%/25-yr amortization factor $690.91 per $100k, break-even occupancy by bisection) matches NOI 145,740, value 2,082,000, debt service 116,073, DSCR 1.2556, max loan at 1.25x 1,406,258 and break-even 79.99% to the cent, and all 25 tests pass. It misses the bar on claims and verification: the headline promise of the loan a lender would give is only shown when the deal fails 1.25x, the cap-rate grid rounds a 7.25% input to 7.3% so the user's own cap rate is missing from it, and 4 of 6 seeded mutants (every finding threshold) survive. A senior underwriter would also want debt yield and lesser-of loan sizing.
